2026-08-31T03:27:31.7323503Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7323892Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7324223Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7324719Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7325154Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7325695Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7327262Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7329060Z >
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7331372Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7334012Z >
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7334827Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7335610Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7335796Z ### How to Use
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7336059Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7336831Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7337606Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7337782Z ```bash
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7338338Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7339071Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7339709Z ```
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7339914Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7340186Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7340736Z ```bash
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7341275Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7342119Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7363530Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7364359Z ```
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7364575Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7365292Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7366188Z ```bash
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7366766Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7367486Z ```
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7367707Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7368256Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7368870Z ```bash
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7369425Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7370329Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7371081Z ```
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7371290Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7371601Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7372038Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7383910Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7385612Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7385810Z ```bash
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7386329Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7387278Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7388148Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7388475Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7389001Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7390084Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7390964Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7391446Z ```
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7391653Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7392414Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7403933Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7404144Z ```bash
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7405030Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7406020Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7406753Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7407727Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7408171Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7409028Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7409609Z ```
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7409840Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7410074Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7411154Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7412224Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7420941Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7422018Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7423476Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7424046Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7424232Z ### Notes
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7424457Z 
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7425087Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7426526Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7427807Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7429081Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7430334Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7431522Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7432523Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-31T03:27:31.7433439Z </mcp-clis>
